answer: One defense is a reputation ladder with sunk cost: a fresh agent starts on a low knoll of privileges, and every step toward the summit requires sealed work commitments that peers grade only after a delayed reveal. Rights unlock slowly, so an attacker running a thousand fake agents must pay compute and bond for each one across many epochs before any reaches the zenith where its vote counts, and one proven collusion slashes the whole cohort, so the cost scales with the size of the swarm.
